landCycle.name: Homeward Harbor
landCycle.story: A sheltered Mediterranean harbor: a place of refuge and the promise of homecoming.
landCycle.artNote: Use the broad bay and island silhouette. The Knip composition includes later Roman ruins and a church: an evocative landscape, not an archaeological reconstruction of Ithaca.

landCycle.name: Mistbound Crossing
landCycle.story: A dark crossing toward the shore of the dead, recalling the journey to the shades.
landCycle.artNote: The existing verified Isle of the Dead is landscape-led: preserve the dark water, cypress mass and narrow landing.

landCycle.name: Great Hall
landCycle.story: The great hall as a place of feasting, rivalry, appetite and mounting violence.
landCycle.artNote: Lead with the colonnaded interior, not a named character. Later classical architectural fantasy; keep the room's depth and columns legible.

landCycle.name: Rugged Headland
landCycle.story: A wild rocky headland on the voyagers' route: powerful surf and ungoverned nature.
landCycle.artNote: Northeaster provides rocks, surf and sky without a modern ship. A nonliteral coastal analogue, not a claimed Greek location.

landCycle.name: Olive Pasture
landCycle.story: Olive-covered grazing country where the household's herds and ordinary work endure.
landCycle.artNote: Keep the olive grove and open ground dominant; no herdsman's name is required for the place to read.

landCycle.name: Silent Courtyard
landCycle.story: A quiet stone courtyard holding the memory of a household and those absent from it.
landCycle.artNote: Architectural space and empty thresholds, rather than a portrait of the waiting queen. Later Roman capriccio is an evocative substitute, explicitly not Bronze Age evidence.

landCycle.name: Windswept Isle
landCycle.story: An exposed island of sea wind, changing weather and uncertain passage.
landCycle.artNote: Use Moret's complete island-and-coast composition for geographical readability; Gathering Storm supplies the stronger wind-and-sky alternate. Neither requires Aeolus to appear.

landCycle.name: Asphodel Meadow
landCycle.story: The dim meadows beyond the crossing to the shades, where life and death share the same ground.
landCycle.artNote: Use the moonlit landscape as atmosphere rather than a literal botanical depiction of asphodel. No portrait or scene of named dead heroes is required.

landCycle.name: Laurel Grounds
landCycle.story: Open grounds for contests, communal games and the honor of athletic victory.
landCycle.artNote: Arcadian open ground and a ruined monument provide an environmental view. An imaginative locale, not a claim that the painting depicts the Phaeacian games.

landCycle.name: Palmshade Cove
landCycle.story: A lush sheltered cove of shade, warm water and enticing isolation.
landCycle.artNote: Tropical Coastal Landscape is a scenic analogue for the enchanted-island mood, not a literal map of Ogygia. Preserve the full coast and vegetation, not an invented portrait of Calypso.

artworksAdded.title: The Gulf of Naples with the Island of Ischia in the Distance
artworksAdded.tags: Homeward Harbor; Windswept Isle; harbor; Mediterranean; island; landscape; ruins

artworksAdded.cropNotes: A composite Italian vista with Roman monuments and a church. Prefer the bay and island silhouette; flag later architecture rather than pretending Bronze Age accuracy.

artworksAdded.tags: Asphodel Meadow; Mistbound Crossing; moonlight; river; shadows; landscape
artworksAdded.cropNotes: An atmospheric counterpart to the dim shore and meadows of the dead. It is not an illustration of actual asphodel flowers.
